name: 2009 Prairie Avenue — the Max A. Meyer house, Burnham & Root's French Gothic rowhouse (T-1913; detailing T-1914)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Max A Meyer Residence. Built 1888'.

research_note: Refined in place from the district draft (T-2352) onto the K01 frontage assembly by T-1913, the envelope package of the T-1837 programme: the outline off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size, and the front's storeys, openings, oriel and ogee gable off the undated Chicagology photograph of 2009-2011 Prairie, cross-checked against Harriet Monroe's 1896 plate. T-1914 owns the carving (the oriel's frieze and apron, the door's surround and finials, the gable's crest and pendant) and the image gate. Liberty L-k01-2009-meyer-1913.

documented_range.note: Built 1888 (the marker) and drawn on the 1911 sheet, which the T-1842 census rules present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The record claims the 1904 target to the sheet's date and no more.

position.symbolic_location: 2009 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2009 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body on its north side, read off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size (px 1055, 393: the outline's own dark line) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this copy. The draft's corner stood 0.13 m behind and 1.67 m south of this one: its rectangle fit stopped where the sheet's printed '2½B' and 'D' bite the traced outline. Rotation 179.389 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body, the 2½B brick block the sheet draws across the lot from the north passage to the party line with 2011: 26.02 m from the rear wall (px 1055) to the front (px 915) and 7.56 m along the front (rows 393-433.7), read at full size off the raster's own outline. The register's published 27 by 82 ft lead (8.2 by 25.0 m) is close but is not a survey; the sheet's 24.8 by 85.4 ft stands. The draft drew it 5.5 m wide because the trace takes the printed numerals for bites out of the house.

stories.note: The sheet prints '2½B': two full storeys and a half. The photograph shows three tiers of street windows over the basement, the third (the paired light at 9.6-11.45 m) in a low storey whose side walls stop at the kneelers' 11.3 m, under the roof's slope: the sheet's half storey. K01 counts it a storey of 2.1 m.

construction.note: The photograph: a rough, deeply textured brick front over a rock-faced brownstone basement, stone dressings and string courses; the sheet colours the building brick ('2½B', pink). The register names the brick 'rough red-brown' and the basement and copings brownstone.

principal_floor_m.note: The door's threshold at y 1530 px, 1.95 m over the wall's foot at the photograph's 100 px a metre, taken at 2.0 m so the stoop climbs it in twelve whole risers (K01's and K07's alike); the stoop rises to it straight from the walk. Above the contract's starting range (0.8-1.8 m), which a source may pass.

storey_heights_m.note: Floors read from the photograph's openings and courses: the oriel's corbel foot at 5.05 m and its lights' sill at 6.0 m put the second floor at about 5.3 m; the string course at 9.1 m and the paired light's sill at 9.6 m the third at about 9.2 m; the kneeler stone at the north corner (11.35-11.95 m) the side walls' head at about 11.3 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front on a stone basement: a starting thickness from the contract's masonry range; no source measures it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A 13 in brick side wall, the contract's ordinary masonry thickness; no source measures it.

service_wall_brick.note: The side and rear walls in the K03 common brick of the avenue's other K01 houses: the photograph shows the north wall darker than the front's face brick but no closer than that.

stone_front.note: The photograph's basement: rock-faced coursed stone from the walk to about 1.25 m, a smooth band over it, and the brick beginning on the stone sill course at about 1.9 m (y 1535 px), the ground-floor light's sill standing on it. The register calls it brownstone; the print is monochrome, so the colour is the register's. T-3365: the base's top re-read at 2x with the contrast stretched (x 380-1160 px, y 1440-1760 px): the rock-faced courses run to about 1.26 m (y 1599 px), three courses of about 0.45 m, the lights' heads under the top one; over them a smooth band to about 1.83 m (y 1542 px) under a thin ledge at about 1.85 m. Laid as three rusticated courses of 0.46 m to 1.38 m and a smooth coping of 0.46 m (the dressed trim's deepest course) to 1.84 m, where K01 had laid two courses to 0.85 m and a 0.4 m coping to 1.25 m: the band's foot stands about 0.12 m over the print's, its top on it.

street_front_brick.note: The front's brick reads in the photograph as a rough, clinker-like face with deep joints, darker than the stone; the register names it 'rough red-brown brick'. K03's rough red-brown panel, as 1918 Prairie's front.

street_front_trim.note: Stone lintels over the street lights, under the surrounds street_front_windows names; the photograph's moulded hoods and the oriel's carved frieze are T-1914's (the facade's detailing).

wall_head.note: No cornice across the front: the photograph carries the front straight up into its gable, with only the string course at 9.1 m across it.

roof_form.note: The photograph shows slate slopes rising behind the gable on the north side; the roof's own form is not seen beyond that. A hip front to back behind the street gable, as 1625 Prairie's (K01's shaped gable stands before a hip's street slope).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The contract's ordinary band; the photograph sees only the north slope's lower edge.

eave_overhang_m.note: A plain eave over the north wall, where the photograph shows a shallow moulded cornice at the far stack; its depth is not read.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing before the door, its depth unread: the photograph sees the flight end-on from the north.

stoop_width_m.note: The flight between its stone cheek walls: about 1.6-1.9 m across in the photograph, whose camera sees it obliquely, so its width is read loosely.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the front's south end (K01's north, the house facing west): the photograph and Monroe's 1896 plate both show the stoop and the arched door beside the party wall with 2011.

front_bays.note: Two bays, read along the front from its north corner (x 390 px) at 100 px a metre: the window column (the ground light, the oriel and the paired light over it) centred at 2.98 m, the door at 6.18 m.

side_bays.note: The north wall's windows (K01's south wall), from the rear: the photograph shows a tall light on the north wall about 1.4 m behind the front corner (x 355-390 px, seen edge-on) and lights farther back it cannot place; the two behind the projection are reconstructed at an even spacing.

rear_bays.note: No source sees the rear wall; two lights a storey, the rowhouse's ordinary rear.

sash_by_storey.note: The side and rear lights: the photograph's north-wall light is too foreshortened to measure, so the kit's ordinary sash, shortened in the low third storey.

street_front_windows.note: Every street light read off the photograph at 100 px a metre from the north corner and the wall's foot: the ground floor's window, two lights on a mullion under a transom, at 2.98 m, 2.05 m clear, from 2.0 to about 4.4 m (built 2.25 m high, its head 0.15 m under the print's, so it clears the oriel's corbel); the small square-headed light beside the oriel at 6.32 m, 0.46 m across, 6.3-7.35 m; and the third storey's paired light at 4.02 m, 2.5 m across its two lights, 9.6-11.45 m. Each stands in a stone surround of long and short blocks, as the photograph shows round all three (K01's quoined surround, its returns and lintel the kit's). The oriel's three lights are its own (bays). T-1914: the carved panels over the door, between its pilasters (x 935-1125 px, about 4.5-5.2 m), under a thin course at about 5.25 m that runs across the front: a carved course of rings 4.8-5.3 m over the door (carved_bands, s 5.4-7.2 m), the print's foliage drawn as the kit's guilloche; T-3365: the carving is laid as a panel over the door's run alone (carved_bands panel, 4.65-5.25 m, s 5.4-7.2 m, its foot the pilasters' capitals), the brick running on beside it where K01 had laid a 0.5 m course across the whole front; the print's thin course at about 5.25 m (about 0.1 m) is not laid. T-3365: the north corner (x 380-440 px, read at 2x with the contrast stretched): brick from the stone sill course to the string course, then a pale stone strip about 0.5 m across from the string course's top (9.2 m, y 810 px) to the kneeler (11.75 m), one bed joint read near its middle; laid as stone courses about 0.6 m deep (corner_stone), their 0.3 m return on the north flank reconstructed (the camera sees the flank edge-on). T-3365: base_top_m 1.84, the smooth band's top read off the print (y 1542 px), where it had been 1.25 m.

basement_lights.note: T-3365: the basement's three square lights under the ground window, read off the photograph at 100 px a metre from the north corner (x 390 px) and the wall's foot (y 1725 px): x 547-625, 655-728 and 760-830 px, so centres 1.96, 3.02 and 4.05 m, each about 0.7-0.78 m across between rock-faced piers, from about 0.08 m over the walk (y 1718 px) to 0.93 m (y 1632 px); built 0.77 m high, their heads 0.08 m under the print's, in the rusticated base's lowest two courses, the third course running over them under the coping as the print's does. Their sills stand above the walk, so no area well is dug (window_kit's area light, well false); the print shows each as a dark opening, its glazing unread, so the kit's fixed basement light is laid in it.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the oriel's three lights, read off the photograph: each about 0.9-1.1 m between its stone mullions (built 0.75 m clear in frames 1.0 m across, 1.05 m apart, so three fit its 3.2 m front), from 6.0 to 8.25 m over the walk, a transom at about 7.5 m

bays.note: The 'slightly bowed window group' of the register: a shallow bowed oriel on the street front over the ground-floor window, read off the photograph: 3.45 m across its stone frame (x 515-860 px), carried on a corbelled apron from 5.05 m, its three lights 6.0-8.25 m, a carved frieze over them to about 8.9 m and its cap at the string course (9.2 m). Its depth is not measurable square on: a flat front 3.2 m across with short cants to the wall, 0.38 m out on three corbel courses (their foot at 4.7 m, the photograph's at about 5.05 m), as Monroe's plate shows it standing a little proud; the register's 'slightly bowed' group is drawn canted, the kit's bow being too deep for three lights this wide. The carved frieze and apron are T-1914's. The north wall's projection: the sheet draws the main body's north line stepping out 1.3 m for 5.86 m, from 5.85 to 11.71 m behind the front (px 946-978, rows 386-393), read at full size; it rises to the wall head, where the photograph's camera puts a cornice on the north flank about 12 m up behind the front (y 715 px). A light a storey in its outer face is reconstructed. T-1914: the oriel's carved frieze over its lights (the print's about 8.3-8.9 m, under its moulded cap at 9.2 m) as a 0.75 m carved band round the oriel under its cap (cap_band), the print's foliage in three cartouches drawn as the kit's guilloche rings; the carved apron under the lights is still plain.

shaped_gable.note: The ogee gable, the front carried up past the side walls into a concave-sided spire, read off the photograph at 100 px a metre: its coped outline's half-width at ten heights (the average of its two sides, about 1.86 m at 12.65 m, 1.24 m at 13.65 m, 0.83 m at 14.65 m, 0.51 m at 15.65 m), widened about 0.15 m through its middle where the render laid over the print through its camera stood inside the print's outline on both sides, rising to a flat top about 0.8 m across at about 16.3 m (the print's about 0.85 m) (the print's left shoulder at y 97 px, 16.30 m), on which the carved crest stands; it leaves the front's full width at the kneeler stone (11.4 m). Its two attic lights (a pair on a mullion, 0.62 m across, 13.75-14.57 m) under the apex. The north side's flare stops on the kneeler at 11.4 m where the south side runs on down to about 10.3 m over the party wall; the kit draws both sides alike (liberty). T-3365: the crest is the print's carved block, not a turned finial: read at 6x with its contrast stretched, a stone about 0.6 m across (x 765-826 px) standing from the coping's inner line at about 16.07 m (y 120 px) to about 16.39 m (y 88 px), its top scrolled in two lobes either side of a boss between; drawn as K01's crest form, its three lobes the envelope of its top and each lobe's eye a boss (the carving's foliage itself is not drawn: liberty). The carved pendant over the paired light stays T-1914's.

roof_covering.note: The photograph shows slate on the north slope behind the gable.

chimneys.note: The register's 'tall chimneys': the photograph shows a tall brick stack with a corbelled cap rising from the north flank, which its camera puts on the north wall about 2.2 m behind the front, its top about 17.4 m up (1.7 m over the ridge); Monroe's plate draws a second, lower stack farther back on the same side, stood here in the north wall's projection. The far stack at the photograph's left edge (x 130-210 px) lies north of this lot through the camera and is read as 2005's. K01 stands a stack inside the main body (0.7 m in from the north wall), so the near stack stands about 0.6 m south of where the photograph puts it; both share one height.

rainwater.note: One pipe down the north wall near the front; the photograph shows none on the front.

window_kit.note: The photograph's lights: the ground window two lights on a mullion under a transom, the third storey's two on a mullion, the small light a sash.

entrance_kit.note: A panelled door up a straight stoop between stone cheek walls, as the photograph shows. T-1914 reads the entrance off the photograph at 100 px a metre from the north corner and the wall's foot: one dark leaf, 1.08 m across (x 957-1065 px, s 5.68-6.76 m), from the principal floor to a transom bar at about 3.8 m (y 1345 px); over the bar a fanlight of two lights parted by a mullion (the print's Y-tracery) in an elliptical head springing at about 4.05 m and rising to its crown at about 4.3 m (y 1295 px), so a rise of about 0.25 m, 0.23 of the span; a moulded stone ring round the head and down the jambs, about 0.23 m broad to its outer edge at about 4.53 m (y 1272 px); and a stone pilaster each side, about 0.25 m broad (x 917-942 and 1110-1135 px), under a capital. Built as K07's arched entrance in the record's elliptical head (entrance_kit.arch), hung with one leaf under a two-light fanlight on its bar 0.25 m under the spring (fanlight_transom), the leaf in a dark varnish as the print's reads near black. T-3365, read at 3x with its contrast stretched: each pilaster runs on over its capital as a slender shaft (about 0.12 m) up through the carved panel to the thin course at about 5.25 m (y 1200 px), under a small spire to about 5.6 m (y 1163-1167 px); over the arch's crown a stem (about 0.08 m) rises to the same course under a bud about 0.23 m across (x 1010-1033 px) to about 5.7 m (y 1155 px). Built as K01's door pinnacles (arch.pilasters.pinnacles): plain shafts, caps and four-sided spires, the crown a turned bud; the print's crockets and the shafts' tapering lower stage are not modelled (liberty). The keystone is the kit's smallest: the print shows none under the moulding.

boundary.note: The photograph shows no fence across the front, only a low coped stone wall on the street line, read through its camera (the street line 7.0 m before the front, where the parcel's street corner stands): about 0.47 m high from about 0.6 m to 5.4 m along the lot (built to 5.25 m, clear of the walk), stopping short of the front walk to the stoop and of the north passage. Its thickness and chamfer are the kit's.

yard.note: The walk to the stoop in stone flags, as the avenue's other K01 fronts.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's 'rear1B': a one-storey brick range behind the house, 7.6 m from the main body's rear wall to its own, 5.98 m across from 1.58 m inside the north wall to the party line, joined to the house along the party line by a 1.4 m neck (the sheet leaves a 1.4 m court between the two elsewhere). Read at full size off the raster. Its height, roof and openings are reconstructed.
